description: AI Village explores the intersection of artificial intelligence and information security. Talks cover adversarial machine learning, evasion techniques against ML-based malware detectors, deep reinforcement learning vulnerabilities, and privacy-preserving model architectures.

talks.title: A Dive into Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning
talks.teaser: Examines privacy-preserving machine learning techniques, homomorphic encryption, and differential privacy safeguards.
talks.summary:
In this technical exploration from the DEF CON Safe Mode AI Village, researchers Daniel and Farhad deliver "Secrets Are Lies, Sharing Is Caring, Privacy Is Theft," examining privacy vulnerabilities in machine learning architectures. Opening at 00:13, the speakers address how trained models frequently leak sensitive training data through output statistics and prediction probabilities.

At 01:00 and 02:00, the presentation examines the delicate balance between machine learning utility and data privacy, evaluating how much model accuracy must be traded off to achieve robust data confidentiality. At 03:00 and 04:00, the authors review classic linkage attacks, citing Latanya Sweeney's landmark re-identification of medical records and the de-anonymization of the Netflix Prize dataset.

The speakers explore modern privacy-preserving frameworks past 10:00, detailing the mathematical mechanics of Differential Privacy, homomorphic encryption, and secure multi-party computation to protect models against membership inference attacks. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Project Domino: Citizen Data Science Against COVID Misinformation
talks.teaser: Details Project Domino, an open-source citizen data science effort leveraging NLP to track COVID-19 misinformation.
talks.summary:
Leo Meyerovich, founder and CEO of Graphistry, introduces Project Domino in the AI Village, an open-source citizen data science initiative analyzing the mechanics and propagation of COVID-19 health misinformation across social media networks [00:04, 05:34].

Meyerovich details how the project combines GPU-accelerated graph visualization with automated data pipelines to expose coordinated inauthentic behavior, bot networks, and terms-of-service abuse on platforms like Twitter [11:11, 16:32]. He demonstrates how transitioning from basic keyword filtering to semantic natural language processing (NLP) and graph community clustering enables researchers to track mutating conspiracy narratives and build proactive defensive alerting systems [22:08, 27:37].

talks.title: Fawkes: Facial Recognition Privacy Protection
talks.teaser: Examines Fawkes, an image cloaking tool that adds pixel-level perturbations to photos to deceive facial recognition models.
talks.summary:
In this community discussion from the DEF CON Safe Mode AI Village, researchers and participants explore Fawkes, an adversarial machine learning privacy framework developed by the University of Chicago to counter unauthorized facial recognition surveillance. Opening at 00:01, the panel introduces the software's mission to protect individuals against mass scraping by commercial facial recognition vendors.

At 02:00, the speakers explain the concept of "adversarial examples for good," showing how Fawkes introduces imperceptible pixel-level perturbations ("cloaks") into portrait photos. These perturbations shift internal feature representations in deep neural networks, causing facial recognition models to incorrectly classify the subject without distorting the image for human viewers.

At 15:00 and 39:00, the panel evaluates the system's real-world resilience, analyzing how cloaked images poison training pipelines when scraped from public social media profiles. The session concludes by discussing model transferability, perturbation boundaries, and defensive countermeasures against image pre-filtering. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Hyperlocal Drift Detection with Goko
talks.teaser: Demonstrates Goko, an algorithm and tool for detecting fine-grained, localized concept drift in production ML models.
talks.summary:
A machine learning researcher presents Goko in the AI Village, an open-source algorithmic tool designed for hyperlocal real-time drift detection across streaming data in production machine learning systems [00:04, 07:34]. The talk addresses the challenge of concept and covariate drift, where shifting input distributions quietly degrade model accuracy over time without triggering traditional error flags.

The speaker introduces Goko's core architecture, which leverages cover tree data structures and k-nearest neighbors to construct computationally efficient topological representations of reference data distributions [12:38, 12:45]. Benchmarking against the EMBER open-source malware dataset, the presentation demonstrates how Goko conducts rapid, streaming inference to detect adversarial perturbations and distribution anomalies in real time with minimal computational overhead [17:40, 23:01].

talks.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: Attacking AMSI Providers
talks.teaser: Hands-on workshop demonstrating adversarial evasion techniques targeting ML-based Antimalware Scan Interface providers.
talks.summary:
In this deep technical dive from the DEF CON Safe Mode AI Village, researcher Rob examines adversarial evasion techniques targeting machine-learning-based Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) providers. Opening at 00:01, Rob explores the fundamental mathematics behind AI-driven endpoint detection engines and how they classify suspicious execution payloads.

At 22:02, the talk contrasts rigid signature-based scanning with modern ML classifiers, demonstrating how slight structural modifications to file headers and magic bytes can break parser interpretation. At 44:02, Rob explores token-level adversarial perturbations, identifying specific byte sequences and keywords that Windows Defender tags as high-risk indicators and showing how to mask malicious scripts while preserving runtime functionality.

Moving past 01:06:00, the speaker demonstrates gradient-based evasion attacks against production ML models. Concluding at 01:28:01, Rob offers practical advice for malware defense engineers to harden ML classifiers against evasion by integrating adversarial examples into training pipelines. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Detecting Social Engineering Emails with a Bleeding-Edge Neural Model
talks.teaser: Presents a cutting-edge deep neural network architecture designed to detect subtle social engineering patterns in emails.
talks.summary:
Joshua Saxe and Younghoo Lee of Sophos AI present an advanced neural language modeling architecture for identifying sophisticated, hand-crafted social engineering and spear-phishing emails in the AI Village [00:02, 00:06]. The researchers explain that targeted spear-phishing attacks deliberately evade traditional heuristics and spam filters by adopting authentic conversational tones and avoiding known malicious links or keywords [08:07].

The speakers contrast classical natural language processing models—such as Bag-of-Words and discrete Markov models—with multi-layer transformer architectures [15:57, 24:06]. They demonstrate how multi-head self-attention mechanisms capture subtle contextual relationships, deceptive framing, and conversational coercion cues [24:12, 36:12], evaluating detection benchmarks across enterprise datasets and exploring future directions using large generative models like GPT-3 [36:20, 49:06].
